title: Between last error and actual throwing we have the useless backoff applied.

body:
If I understand the implementation of exponential backoff correctly, then it grows surprisingly fast with the default `delay`:

| Retry | Wait        | 
|-------|-------------|
| 1     | 0.1 seconds |
| 2     | 10 seconds  |
| 3     | ~17 minutes |
| 4     | ~27 hours   |
| 5     | ~4 months   |

With the default `timeout` of 60 seconds, only three attempts will be made:
- The original attempt.
- The first retry after 100ms.
- The second retry after another 10 seconds.

Would it make sense to document this surprisingly fast growth?
Perhaps even implement `EXPONENTIAL2` with two as the base, kind of like what is discussed [here](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/exponential-backoff-and-jitter/)?

I have seen a few instances of code like `{ retries: 5, backoff: 'EXPONENTIAL' }`, which suggests the author did not expect the current behavior (because the `retries` is redundant; only two retries will ever be done before the timeout is reached).
title: Exponential backoff grows surprisingly fast
